title: Edit repos/development-vessel/src/resolvers/feature-compose.ts so the compose trace emission keeps the execution identif
description:
Edit repos/development-vessel/src/resolvers/feature-compose.ts so the compose trace emission keeps the execution identifier the trace store returns.

The trace emission is the fetch call in this file whose URL path is v2/activities/executions. It is written as `void fetch(`, so its promise is never awaited and its response is thrown away. The trace store replies with a JSON body shaped `{ success: true, data: { execution_id: "..." } }`. That returned execution_id is the identifier of the row this emission just created, and it is the only address by which the row can later be graded. Discarding it is the whole defect: 894 of 899 compose rows carry a null verdict because the grader addresses a different, synthesised identifier that matches no row.

Required edits, both inside this one file:

1. Immediately above the `try {` that encloses that fetch, declare `let traceExecutionId: string | null = null;`.
2. Turn that `void fetch(` into an awaited call. Read the parsed JSON body and, when `data.execution_id` is a non-empty string, assign it to traceExecutionId. Keep `signal: AbortSignal.timeout(5000)` unchanged, keep the trailing `.catch(...)`, and keep the enclosing `catch`, so any trace-store failure still leaves traceExecutionId null and can never fail or delay a compose. The enclosing function is already async.
3. In the returned report body, directly beneath the line starting `restored_files: restored.map`, insert `trace_execution_id: traceExecutionId,`.

Edit 3 is what makes edits 1 and 2 live; without it the variable is unused and the identifier is still thrown away. Do not modify the BUSY or error verdict payloads — those are not the trace emission. Do not touch any other file.
